title: Fold a Chain: Interleave Front and Reversed Back Halves
statement: You are given a list of integer values that represent a singly linked list chained head-to-tail, e.g. values[0] is the head and values[-1] is the tail. Reorder the chain by folding its back half onto its front half: transform [v0, v1, v2, ..., vn-2, vn-1] into [v0, vn-1, v1, vn-2, v2, vn-3, ...], and return the reordered values as a plain list of ints. Concretely, you interleave the original order (v0, v1, v2, ...) with the reversed order (vn-1, vn-2, vn-3, ...), always taking from the front first, until every node has been placed exactly once. For an odd number of values the single middle element ends up last. Solve it as the classic three-step in-place linked-list composite in O(1) extra space: (1) find the middle using fast/slow pointers, (2) reverse the second half in place, (3) merge the two halves alternately. Do not build a reversed copy of the whole list or walk two indices across a single array in place of real pointer surgery. If the input has length 0 or 1, return it unchanged.
reference_solution:
class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


def fold_reorder(values):
    if len(values) <= 1:
        return list(values)
    dummy = ListNode()
    curr = dummy
    for v in values:
        curr.next = ListNode(v)
        curr = curr.next
    head = dummy.next
    slow = fast = head
    while fast.next and fast.next.next:
        slow = slow.next
        fast = fast.next.next
    second = slow.next
    slow.next = None
    prev = None
    curr = second
    while curr:
        nxt = curr.next
        curr.next = prev
        prev = curr
        curr = nxt
    second = prev
    first = head
    while second:
        f_next = first.next
        s_next = second.next
        first.next = second
        second.next = f_next
        first = f_next
        second = s_next
    out = []
    node = head
    while node:
        out.append(node.val)
        node = node.next
    return out
hints: This is not one trick but three chained together. If you split the chain in half, what would you have to do to the back half so that reading it forward gives you vn-1, vn-2, vn-3, ...?

Use fast/slow pointers to land slow on the last node of the first half, cut the list there (slow.next = None), reverse the detached second half in place, then weave the two halves together one node at a time starting from the front.

The subtle failure is the cut: after the fast/slow loop, the second half must START at slow.next and the first half must be terminated with slow.next = None. If the middle node stays attached to both halves, an odd-length list emits its middle value twice (and a real pointer version forms a cycle). Merge by repeatedly saving first.next and second.next, then setting first.next = second and second.next = saved first.next, advancing both.
